task: real-code audit of a seeded Convex module (10 planted issues + 2 correct functions as false-positive bait)
secondary_metric: false positives per run (lower is better)

per_issue_baseline_recall._legend: how many of the 6 baseline runs (across all tiers) caught each planted issue, vs the 6 with_skill runs

P7_floating_promise_rule1.role: control — everyone spots the un-awaited patch

P6_no_access_control_rule6.role: minor — both Haiku baselines missed it

P2_filter_on_query_rule2.role: discriminator — Sonnet baselines & one Haiku never flagged byAuthor

P10_cron_internal_rule7.role: discriminator — baselines call it an 'undefined function', missing the public-vs-internal point

P8_runaction_same_runtime_rule9.role: hard — only Opus baselines; both Haiku WITH skill still missed it

P9_sequential_runquery_rule10.role: discriminator — baselines flag latency/null-deref, not the inconsistent snapshot

P4_date_now_in_query_rule13.role: STRONG discriminator — BOTH Opus baselines missed it, distracted by the adjacent createdAt .filter

P3_unbounded_collect_rule3.role: STRONGEST discriminator — no baseline flagged byAuthor's unbounded .collect as a distinct issue

findings: Recall climbs monotonically with model size at baseline (Haiku 0.35 < Sonnet 0.55 < Opus 0.70); the skill lifts every tier to >=0.80 and Sonnet/Opus to a perfect 10/10.

The .paginate() .filter exception is the dominant false positive: every Sonnet and Opus BASELINE run (4/4) flagged the correct myMessages function as a .filter violation — the same item-7 blind spot from iterations 1-2, now causing wrong review comments on real code. with_skill drove FPs to 0 at Haiku/Sonnet (agents explicitly named the exception); Opus had one hedged residual.

Real code is harder than the quiz: BOTH Opus baselines MISSED Date.now() (P4) here — they saw the neighbouring `.filter` and flagged that, overlooking that `cutoff = Date.now()` is the bug. In iteration-1's quiz Opus got Date.now 3/3. The skill restored it to 6/6.

P3 (unbounded .collect, 0/6 baseline) and P9 (sequential-runQuery inconsistency, 1/6) and P4 (1/6) are the issues the skill adds most on; P8 (runAction) is the one even skilled Haiku still misses (4/6 with_skill).

Precision watch-item (not scored as FP): the rule-6 'every public function needs access control' non-negotiable makes skilled agents flag EVERY public read query for missing auth. On a real codebase with legitimately-public reads that is noise — the skill could distinguish mutations/PII reads (must-auth) from public reads.
